name: Warehouse Dock Infiltration Loss
applicable_contexts: heating or cooling climate duty plausible
trigger_conditions: dock count or door-cycle profile unresolved
physical_basis: Dock doors create air exchange losses that scale with door-open time, seal condition and temperature differential.
operational_basis: Door discipline, staging rhythm, scheduling and loading practices can dominate thermal losses at the logistics interface.
financial_mechanism: HVAC or refrigeration cost can be driven by logistics-interface losses rather than equipment efficiency.
typical_false_assumption: HVAC inefficiency is the primary source of visible energy pressure.
hypothesis: If dock activity and conditioned or refrigerated space are material, losses may be driven by dock-interface behavior rather than generic HVAC inefficiency.
minimum_evidence_to_confirm: dock seals or door management evidence suggests leakage risk
falsification_conditions: strong documented dock seal and door-management program
profile and weather do not support dock-driven loss framing
allowed_claim_language: Dock infiltration is a structurally plausible loss mode requiring targeted falsification.
prohibited_claim_language: The asset is losing energy through docks.
financial_exposure_if_true: HVAC CAPEX may target the wrong variable
refrigeration or HVAC economics may be misframed
operational changes may outperform equipment-first framing
financial_exposure_if_false: attention should shift to competing drivers
stop_conditions: temperature duty bounded enough to rank the hypothesis
escalation_conditions: operator dock-cycle confirmation required after public evidence fails
field seal-condition evidence needed if public and operator evidence remain weak
example_outputs: Before buying equipment, determine whether the building is leaking conditioned air through its logistics interface.
tests: warehouse acceptance bundle should activate this as plausible when dock activity and conditioned duty remain unresolved
no observed-loss language allowed without local evidence
